function.name: generate_sea_foam
function.description: Simulates the creation of sea foam based on the agitation level of water, amount of organic material, and the presence of salt. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

agitation_level.description: The level of agitation in the water, represented by a scale from 1 (calm) to 10 (very agitated).

organic_material.description: The amount of organic material present in grams per liter. This is a float type value.

salt_presence.description: Indicates whether salt is present (true) or not (false) in the water.

temperature.description: The water temperature in degrees Celsius. If unspecified, defaults to average sea temperature. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The color of the sea isn’t a single, fixed hue—it changes with depth, light, water composition, and the surrounding environment. Here’s a quick rundown of what you’ll typically see:

| Depth / Conditions | Typical Color | Why it looks that way |
|--------------------|---------------|-----------------------|
| **Shallow, clear water** | Turquoise / aquamarine | Light penetrates easily; the water scatters blue and green wavelengths, giving a bright, almost glass‑like look. |
| **Mid‑depth, calm water** | Deep blue | Blue light penetrates the most; the water absorbs longer wavelengths (red, orange, yellow), leaving a rich blue. |
| **Very deep or murky water** | Dark blue / indigo | Even more absorption of light; the water appears almost black in very deep or turbid conditions. |
| **Near shore with algae or phytoplankton** | Greenish | Chlorophyll in algae absorbs red light and reflects green, tinting the water. |
| **Near a sandy bottom** | Pale blue / light turquoise | The sand reflects some light back, brightening the surface. |
| **Near a rocky or volcanic area** | Grayish or brownish | Suspended minerals or volcanic ash can give the water a muted tone. |
| **Under a storm or high agitation** | White or frothy | Wind and waves create foam, scattering light and making the surface appear white or gray. |

So, while the “classic” image of the sea is a deep blue, the actual color is a dynamic spectrum that depends on many natural factors.
